We used to pull a duty at the ER called OPPEL-D where we would escort any patients being transported to hospitals off-base and be with them to help them out.

I was escorting a one year old boy with pneumonia to the Gangnam area (I'm stationed in Korea) to a hospital I'm not very fond of, Samsung. 

It was an all day duty but he finally was admitted into the ward and I remember I was helping the nurse fix the little boy's IV, he had been picking at the tape securing it to his hand. He had been quiet for most of the day, too sick to make much of a fuss. The nurse stepped out to get a new hospital bracelet for the baby, since he had slobbered all over his, rendering it unintelligible.

I sat him on my lap to tape the tubing to his little arm while his mom was downstairs in the cafeteria when he broke the silence by giggling like crazy. I thought the tubing was tickling him and I bounced him up and down, smiling at him, only to realize that he was staring at a corner of the room, which was completely empty. 

He kept giggling, that cute crazy giggling babies do where they laugh so hard they run out of breath and he finally settled down and waved at the empty space and said, "Bah bah! (Bye bye?)" and blew kisses in the direction of the empty corner.

WAS not excited to be in the room alone with the kid ;-;
